SMTO-EXE-0078 — SMTO lost contact with the computer whose clipboard it was using

GUID: e8077659-8872-503c-bead-332dee988c5d
Slug: clipboard-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't get a usable answer from the Gateway, the helper program on that computer, while working with its clipboard or while cancelling that work.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on, awake and connected to the network. This error usually means the Gateway stopped answering or the network dropped.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. This confirms SMTO can reach the Gateway again before you send new clipboard work.
  3. If you had asked SMTO to copy something or clear the clipboard, paste on that computer (for example into a blank note) to see what it holds now. If contact was lost while SMTO was cancelling, the change may have finished anyway.
  4. Ask SMTO for the clipboard action again only if the clipboard doesn't already hold what you wanted. SMTO never repeats clipboard changes on its own, so you decide whether a new one is needed.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds for that Gateway and your new clipboard request completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't paste your clipboard contents into the report; they may be private.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's clipboard call to the selected Gateway failed in transport (HTTP/outbound error or rejection, or a failed /clipboard/cancel), so no usable receipt was received.

What this means

  • The clipboard route received a Gateway HTTP/transport failure or could not confirm cancellation; request phase determines whether a write could have happened. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The clipboard route received a Gateway HTTP/transport failure or could not confirm cancellation; request phase determines whether a write could have happened.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect status, phase and operation type before reconnecting; keep writes with uncertain effects separate from failed reads.

How to fix it

  • Check the selected node's Gateway connection (Settings › Setup › Gateways, and the Server log for the /clipboard/operation or /clipboard/cancel request). Restore connectivity and refresh Gateway metadata; for a write, clear or failed cancel, verify the original execution_id's clipboard state on that Gateway before issuing a new explicit request, and never replay it automatically.
  • Restore the selected route and inspect the original request's state before new work; read content only when explicitly requested.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconnect the selected Gateway and refresh its metadata before making another explicit read.

How to verify the fix

  • The original request is settled on the same verified Gateway before another deliberate clipboard action.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
